facts.finding: Wrapper execs Python directly, with no wrapper signal trap; installed launchd KeepAlive is true and next launch retains current arguments/configuration.

asyncio Runner installs the deferred first-SIGINT handler only on the main thread if incoming SIGINT handler is default_int_handler. First signal cancels the task; second raises KeyboardInterrupt immediately. Static source cannot prove the live in-process handler.
One synchronous perception cycle completes before its only await. With normal Runner SIGINT handling, pending cancellation is delivered at that await, and main logs a cooperative stop.

Camera native calls have no explicit deadline. Vision HTTP timeout 60s, RASCII timeout 30s, rec timeout 8s and Whisper timeout 60s bound ordinary child/request waits, but do not establish a hard 600s global shutdown deadline.
Whisper can spawn ffmpeg without a subprocess timeout. This is a genuine possible descendant; normal operation decodes the five-second WAV then exits.

Existing subprocess.run timeout or immediate KeyboardInterrupt kills only its direct child and waits. A killed Whisper process does not by itself prove its ffmpeg descendant exited. Under normal first-SIGINT deferred cancellation the parent lets the synchronous subprocess finish.
Authored/persisted perceptions and frames are retained on disk. Startup can rename oldest perception files into archive; it does not delete their content.

Restart resets volatile host ASCII history(max 25), timing and crossfade state, and may immediately schedule fresh camera/vision/audio work. Legacy pause flags point at an absent consciousness-bridge directory, not a currently proven maintenance drain.

preconditions: Finish the independent host observation window first.
Recheck exact perception PID 3895 and process start, command arguments, source/launcher/plist hashes and interpreter resolution.
Create a durable maintenance receipt before signaling. Record unaffected provider/bridge/Minime/Ollama top-level process identities and perception descendants.
reviewed_bounded_plan.action: Send exactly one SIGINT to the verified perception parent only. No process-group signal, bootout, forced kickstart, repeated SIGINT or escalation.
reviewed_bounded_plan.observation: Wait at most 600 seconds for old parent exit and a stable KeepAlive replacement with expected interpreter/arguments. Track descendants during this interval and require no surviving old owned descendants; require fresh expected artifacts/status. Preserve any failure without further signals.
postconditions: Provider, bridge, Minime and top-level Ollama PID/start identities remain unchanged.
No authored history/config/package changes; preserve archive moves produced by normal perception startup.
Measure actual memory-pressure/swap/footprint improvement after settling; no promise of 10.7 GiB physical memory release.
Start a fresh 2 hour passive baseline before MLX qualification because this relevant memory/serving consumer changed.

memory_interpretation.finding: Large retained heap merits a bounded recovery attempt but does not establish a leak or sufficient capacity for another full model. Footprint, resident mappings and swap are overlapping accounting views and must not be summed.

baseline_note: Perception PID/source/plist are absent from the 105 bound identity files and sampled service labels in the initial passive observation; the relevant-service-change policy still requires a fresh baseline.
